How the repository is organised

week-11-managed-prometheus — the important parts; full source on GitHub
week-11-managed-prometheus/
│
├── terraform/      split by the decision each file makes
│   ├── main.tf           the workspace, the identity, the grant on the DCR
│   ├── vm.tf             the Prometheus host — and its egress
│   ├── grafana.tf        the instance, and the read it needs
│   ├── alerts.tf         one recording rule, one alert rule, no cluster
│   └── cloud-init.yaml.tftpl
│                         rendered by Terraform: the only file that
│                         names the ingestion URL and the client id
│
└── scripts/        deploy, validate, cleanup — each runs end to end

# WHY cloud-init IS A TEMPLATE AND NOT A STATIC FILE
#
# The remote_write URL is assembled from the workspace's own data collection
# rule — its metrics ingestion endpoint plus its immutable id. Both are known
# only after apply. Rendering the config means a rebuild in another
# subscription produces a correct prometheus.yml with nothing to hand-edit,
# and means there is no placeholder anyone can forget to replace.
#
# There is also nothing in it to redact before publishing. The `azuread`
# block names a managed identity by client id; a client id is an identifier,
# not a credential.
#
# Full source, including variables and the scripts:
